parameters.query:
-- The published band and the observed practice in one round trip: both are
-- keyed on the same style string and both are needed by the same next node.
-- ⛔ `cohort` carries the RUNG. A cohort that relaxed to a different beer must
-- not be presented to the model as this beer's practice, so `Build propose
-- pack` drops the block entirely above rung 2 rather than caption it.
SELECT coalesce(ref.f_style_bands($1::text), '{}'::jsonb) AS bands,
       (SELECT to_jsonb(c) FROM nlq.find_cohort(
          $1::text, ARRAY(SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text($2::jsonb))) c) AS cohort,
       (SELECT jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(s)) FROM nlq.cohort_stats(
          $1::text, ARRAY(SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text($2::jsonb))) s) AS practice,
       -- Stage B. One verdict per named term -- catalogued / known_uncatalogued
       -- / thin / unknown -- so "is it in the catalogue" stops being a yes/no
       -- that had nowhere to send a no. ⛔ `unknown` is the brewer's business
       -- BEFORE a grain bill is built, not a line in the warnings afterwards.
       (SELECT jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(r)) FROM brew.f_resolve_request(
          ARRAY(SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text($2::jsonb))) r) AS resolved,
       -- C4. How brewers actually use each named ingredient: stage distribution
       -- and amount quantiles, from 141,857 real additions. ⛔ Reported PER UNIT
       -- and never converted -- vanilla arrives as each, oz, tsp, g and lb, and
       -- a quartile over the mixture would be a number about nothing.
       (SELECT jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(ip)) FROM jsonb_array_elements_text($2::jsonb) t
          CROSS JOIN LATERAL nlq.ingredient_practice(t.value, $1::text) ip) AS ing_practice,
       -- C3. Two or three whole recipes from the cohort, past a plausibility
       -- gate. The gate matters: corpus recipe 280784 is a genuine vanilla
       -- lactose stout that records IBU 0.00 beside two 60-minute boil hops.
       (SELECT jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(e)) FROM nlq.find_exemplars(
          $1::text, ARRAY(SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text($2::jsonb))) e) AS exemplars,
       -- ⛔ STYLE ONLY -- no ingredient filter, deliberately. `practice` above is
       -- keyed on style AND every named ingredient, so a brief naming something
       -- rare relaxes the cohort to a higher rung and `Build propose pack` then
       -- drops the whole block rather than caption a different beer's practice.
       -- That is right for PROPORTIONS and wrong for the yeast fallback, which
       -- only ever needs "what do people ferment this style with". Asking the
       -- narrower question separately keeps rung 1 for the style: measured
       -- 2026-09-16, `sweet stout` alone is rung 1 and S-04 at 18.8%, while the
       -- same brief with poppy seeds in it relaxes past rung 2 and yields none.
       (SELECT jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(y)) FROM nlq.cohort_stats($1::text, ARRAY[]::text[]) y
         WHERE y.section = 'yeast') AS style_yeasts;

WITH params AS
  (SELECT 'stout'::text AS family, -- brief.style.value
 '{"aroma":["chocolate","coffee"],"flavour":["sweet"],"mouthfeel":["full","creamy"]}'::JSONB AS sensory, -- brief.sensory
 11::numeric AS abv -- brief.targets.abv.value, or NULL
),
     fam AS
  (SELECT regexp_replace(lower(coalesce(family, '')), '[^a-z0-9]+', '', 'g') AS f
   FROM params),
     hit AS
  (-- family match on name or *-family tag
 SELECT s.id
   FROM ref.styles s,
        fam
   WHERE s.guide = 'BJCP'
     AND fam.f <> ''
     AND (regexp_replace(lower(s.name), '[^a-z0-9]+', '', 'g') LIKE '%' || fam.f || '%'
          OR EXISTS
            (SELECT 1
             FROM unnest(s.tags) t
             WHERE regexp_replace(t, '-?family$|[^a-z0-9]+', '', 'g') = fam.f))),
     pool AS
  (-- the family, or all BJCP styles if the family matched nothing
 SELECT s.*,
        EXISTS
     (SELECT 1
      FROM hit) AS family_match
   FROM ref.styles s
   WHERE s.guide = 'BJCP'
     AND (s.id IN
            (SELECT id
             FROM hit)
          OR NOT EXISTS
            (SELECT 1
             FROM hit))),
     words AS
  (SELECT DISTINCT e.key AS field,
                   lower(btrim(w)) AS word
   FROM params,
        jsonb_each(coalesce(sensory, '{}')) e,
        jsonb_array_elements_text(e.value) w
   WHERE e.key IN ('aroma',
                   'flavour',
                   'appearance',
                   'mouthfeel')
     AND btrim(w) <> ''),
     hits AS
  (-- word found in its own field, overall_impression or tags
 SELECT p.id,
        w.field,
        w.word,
        to_tsvector('english', array_to_string(p.tags, ' ')) @@ plainto_tsquery('english', w.word) AS in_tags
   FROM pool p
   JOIN words w ON to_tsvector('english', concat_ws(' ', CASE w.field
                                                             WHEN 'aroma' THEN p.aroma
                                                             WHEN 'flavour' THEN p.flavor
                                                             WHEN 'appearance' THEN p.appearance
                                                             ELSE p.mouthfeel
                                                         END, p.overall_impression, array_to_string(p.tags, ' '))) @@ plainto_tsquery('english', w.word)),
     rarity AS
  (-- 1 when one style matches the word, 0 when all do
 SELECT field,
        word,
        ln(
             (SELECT count(*)
              FROM pool)::numeric / count(*)) / nullif(ln(
                                                            (SELECT count(*)
                                                             FROM pool)::numeric), 0) AS r
   FROM hits
   GROUP BY field,
            word),
     weighted AS
  (-- a tag hit counts in full: tags are curated and never negated
 SELECT h.id,
        h.field,
        h.word,
        CASE
            WHEN h.in_tags THEN 1
            ELSE coalesce(r.r, 0)
        END AS weight
   FROM hits h
   JOIN rarity r USING (field,
                        word)),
     sens AS
  (SELECT id,
          sum(weight) AS RAW,
          jsonb_object_agg(field, words) AS matched
   FROM
     (SELECT id,
             field,
             sum(weight) AS weight,
             jsonb_agg(word
                       ORDER BY word) AS words
      FROM weighted
      GROUP BY id,
               field) x
   GROUP BY id),
     scored AS
  (SELECT p.*,
          sens.matched,
          params.abv AS target_abv,
          coalesce(sens.raw / nullif(max(sens.raw) OVER (), 0), 0) AS sensory_score,
          CASE
              WHEN params.abv IS NULL
                   OR NOT p.has_vitals THEN NULL
              WHEN params.abv BETWEEN p.abv_min AND p.abv_max THEN 1
              ELSE greatest(0, 1 - greatest(p.abv_min - params.abv, params.abv - p.abv_max) / greatest(p.abv_max - p.abv_min, 1))
          END AS abv_score,
          (p.tags && ARRAY['specialty-beer',
                           'specialtybeer']) AS is_specialty
   FROM pool p
   CROSS JOIN params
   LEFT JOIN sens ON sens.id = p.id)
SELECT id AS ref_style_id,
       code || '. ' || name AS label,
       round(2 * coalesce(abv_score, 0) + sensory_score, 2) AS score,
       family_match,
       ref.f_range_text(abv_min, abv_max) AS abv_range,
       CASE
           WHEN abv_score IS NULL THEN NULL
           WHEN target_abv < abv_min THEN 'below by ' || trim_scale(abv_min - target_abv)
           WHEN target_abv > abv_max THEN 'above by ' || trim_scale(target_abv - abv_max)
           ELSE 'in range'
       END AS abv_fit,
       coalesce(matched, '{}') AS matched,
       overall_impression
FROM scored
ORDER BY is_specialty,
         2 * coalesce(abv_score, 0) + sensory_score DESC,
         code
LIMIT 5;

json.question: I want to make a pastry stout recipe. I want a fairly strong, ~8 percent abv, with vanilla and poppy seeds. It would be representing a famous hungarian dessert called Mákos Guba. The vanilla and crushed poppy seeds would be drenched in rum, and I would add that to the stout. I want a really sweet, thick vanilla custardy stout with poppy seed, which is bitter. I want to use very little hops, to be a drinkable, Liqueur-like sweet treat. I want to make 10 liters of this. Can you provide me ideas, and could we manage to create a new recipe to achieve this result?
